newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end weak after cautious session.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end weak after cautious session.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended weak on Thursday, with fears about higher interest rates keeping investors cautious and prompting some selling in rate sensitive areas, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index fell 36.44 points to 11,040.51. Turnover was HK$3.53 billion compared to HK$3.87 billion on Wednesday.
Analysts said investors were nervously awaiting Friday's U.S. jobs report.
"People are not sticking their necks out ahead of the numbers in the States in case they signal an increase in interest rates," said Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage.
He said if the payroll data were much stronger than expected, stocks could sell off early next week. Investors were likely to remain sidelined on Friday, Gorges added.

"In the short term we are dominated by interest rates. I don't think investors will begin to participate ahead of the weekend. They just prefer to wait and see," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"Most investors continue to stay on the sidelines or take profits in interest rate sensitive stocks like property and banking," he added.

Sun Hung Kai Properties closed the session HK$0.50 lower at HK$74.25 and Cheung Kong fell HK$0.50 to HK$54.00. Henderson Land fell HK$0.25 to HK$60.00 and New World Development slipped HK$0.20 to HK$37.20.
In the banking sector, Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.25 to HK$78.25.
Utilities bucked the weaker trend with HongKong Electric rising HK$0.25 to HK$23.25, China Light adding HK$0.10 to HK$32.40 and Hongkong & China Gas up HK$0.20 to HK$12.85.
Wharf Holdings slipped HK$0.05 to HK$28.90 after rising HK$0.75 on Wednesday following the release of its interim results.
Standard & Poor's affirmed its "A" ratings on Wharf and its guaranteed subsidiaries but said the rating outlook was negative.
SHK Convertibles rose HK$0.20 to HK$7.20. The company posted first half net profit of HK$10.19 million compared to HK$14.13 million and proposed a cash distribution of HK$4.00 per share.
